{"body":"**Priority: High.** Under auto mode, a background worker can push to this public repo with only the auto-mode classifier's judgment in the way.

## Parent

#40

## What to build

A background worker must not be able to push, open a PR, or close an issue on its own. Today nothing stops it. The `~/.claude-mattpocock-hub` profile's `deny` list holds only `Edit(~/.claude/**)`. `/implement` commits to the current branch, and `main` has no branch protection. Under `--permission-mode auto`, the only guard on a push is the auto-mode classifier reading "Any push there is publishing" from `autoMode.environment`. The classifier makes a judgment call each time and enforces no rule. #58 gates the supervisor's actions and leaves its workers ungated.

Design notes:

- A prefix rule like `Bash(git push*)` misses `git -C . push` and similar forms. A PreToolUse hook that parses the command is more reliable.
- The supervisor runs in the same profile as its workers, so a plain profile-wide deny also blocks the supervisor.
- Two candidate routes around that: one allowed script that checks the grant before pushing, or a hook that refuses when the session is in auto mode. Check whether the hook input carries the permission mode.
- Per-session environment variables can't tell workers apart. The daemon pre-spawns "spare" hosts before a launch, so a variable set at launch may never reach the worker.
- Launch flags can't either. Per ADR 0003, a resume that passes any flag, or that targets a still-live session, starts a copy.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] In a background session under auto mode, `git push`, `git -C <dir> push`, `git push` inside a compound command, `gh pr create`, `gh pr merge` and `gh issue close` are refused.
- [ ] The refusal names the grant file (`docs/agents/supervision.md`, see #58) and the supervisor as the route to a shared action.
- [ ] The supervisor can still perform a granted shared action, and #58's grant check is the only route to it.
- [ ] The maintainer's own interactive sessions in the profile can still push.
- [ ] Tests cover each refused form and the granted route.

## Blocked by

None (can start immediately)

input.command:
git commit -S -s --amend \
  -m "Add PreToolUse hook denying shared actions to background workers" \
  -m "A claude --bg background session in auto mode could push, open a PR, or close an issue on its own: main has no branch protection, and the auto-mode classifier only makes a judgment call, not a rule. #58 gates the supervisor's own actions on a standing grant but leaves its workers ungated (#66)." \
  -m "plugins/mp-ported-skills/scripts/deny-shared-actions.sh is a PreToolUse hook, matched on the Bash tool, that refuses git push (including git -C <dir> push, one inside a compound command, and one behind a leading VAR=value or env prefix), gh pr create, gh pr merge and gh issue close. It fires only when the session is unattended (CLAUDE_CODE_SESSION_ATTENDED=0, read from its own process env) and in auto mode (permission_mode in the hook payload), so a maintainer's own interactive session, whatever its permission mode, is never in scope. Both signals and their discovery are recorded in docs/adr/0004-deny-shared-actions-hook-gates-on-attended-and-auto.md, along with the launch-time-variable and launch-flag routes considered and rejected, and the deliberate boundary at sh -c/eval indirection, which this splitter cannot reliably follow without parsing shell quoting." \
  -m "The refusal names docs/agents/supervision.md and the supervisor (#58) as the route to a shared action. supervise's SKILL.md is updated to say a worker's own push attempt is now refused, rather than merely checked for after the fact." \
  -m "tests/deny-shared-actions.test.sh covers each refused form, the env/VAR=value indirection, commands that only resemble a refused form, the maintainer's own attended sessions in any permission mode, an unattended session outside auto mode, a non-Bash tool call, and the sh -c boundary staying uncaught on purpose."
